title: Obtain experimental crystal structures
action: Download the CIF files for Mn₂(CO)₁₀ (CSD refcode MNCO10), Ir₆(CO)₁₆ black (IRCOAL), and Ir₆(CO)₁₆ red (IRCOAL01) from the Cambridge Structural Database. Parse each CIF to extract fractional coordinates, unit cell parameters, space group symmetry, and atomic element types.
description: Collect the experimental crystal structures required as input for the energy calculations.

title: Compute IAM and IEM
action: Implement the Buckingham atom‑atom potential with the following parameters (A in kcal/mol, B in Å⁻¹, C in kcal/mol): O–O (77700, 4.18, 259.40), C–C (71600, 3.68, 421.00), O–C (75700, 3.91, 339.40), Kr–Kr (270600, 3.28, 3628.00), Kr–O (145002, 3.73, 970.10). For each cluster, parse the atomic coordinates. Compute intramolecular energy (IAM) by summing over all non‑bonded atom pairs within the reference molecule, excluding ⟨1‑3⟩ interactions on the same metal; partition into O–O, O–C, C–C repulsive, C–C attractive, and M–O contributions (use Kr proxy for metal atoms). Compute intermolecular energy (IEM) by summing interactions between the reference molecule and all surrounding molecules within 10 Å, applying crystallographic symmetry. For Ir₆(CO)₁₆ black, treat the two independent molecules separately. For Ir₆(CO)₁₆ red, report the total C–C IAM (not split into repulsive/attractive). Record all results in kcal/mol in a structured JSON file.
description: JSON file containing the computed IAM components and total IEM for Mn2(CO)10, Ir6(CO)16 black, and Ir6(CO)16 red.
